items.en: Hormuz oil traffic is down 40 percent: Are Iran's tanker attacks working?
items.zh: 荷姆茲油輪遇襲，通行量暴跌四成
items.summary: Al Jazeera reports vessel crossings through the Strait of Hormuz fell from 226 in the first week of November to 125 in the week of 17-23 November, a drop of more than 40 percent, as Iran presses attacks on shipping. More than 25 tankers were struck in a week, several catching fire after hitting naval mines attributed to Iran. Tehran says the strait stays closed until the US lifts its naval blockade, halts hostilities and waives sanctions, and that owners must coordinate passage with its armed forces. Brent traded near $88 after earlier topping $120; ships now sail dark with transponders off.

items.en: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi attacks after Hodeidah strike
items.zh: 胡塞無人機襲沙烏地，聯軍攔截反擊
items.summary: Saudi Arabia said its air defences destroyed four Houthi drones over Ras Tanura on Wednesday morning and three more over the Eastern Province, a day after the Saudi-led coalition bombed the rebel-held Red Sea port of Hodeidah and targets in Saada and Amran. Coalition spokesman Turki Al-Maliki reported no casualties. The Houthis threatened Saudi Red Sea ports including Jeddah, telling port workers, residents and shipping companies to leave. On Tuesday a Houthi drone hit Riyadh's tallest tower, which houses the Saudi sovereign wealth fund, injuring at least 11 people. Hodeidah is the main lifeline for food reaching millions in northern Yemen.

items.en: Israeli strike kills Hamas official, his wife and children
items.zh: 以軍空襲加薩，哈馬斯官員全家罹難
items.summary: Gaza's Ministry of Interior said an Israeli air attack at dawn on Wednesday destroyed a home in the Shati refugee camp west of Gaza City, killing Muhammad Majid Abu al-Awf, 47, director of the Internal Security Service in northern Gaza, along with his wife Noura, 41, and daughters Yusra, 15, and Jana, 13. The ministry called it a massacre aimed at dismantling Gaza's security apparatus and spreading chaos. It came less than 24 hours after a strike killed the service's director general, Brigadier-General Naim Abu Nahal. Hamas urged ceasefire guarantor states to intervene; at least 1,680 have been killed since October 2025.

items.en: Asia's markets dive as return of Nvidia's Huang fails to quell AI doubts
items.zh: AI 泡沫疑慮重燃，亞股全面重挫
items.summary: Asian equities sold off sharply on Wednesday as doubts about the artificial intelligence boom returned, erasing a rally sparked by Jensen Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia chief executive. South Korea's Kospi led losses, down 6.2 percent, while Taiwan's Taiex closed 4.8 percent lower after falling more than 8 percent intraday; Japan's Nikkei 225 shed 2.8 percent and Hong Kong's Hang Seng 1.1 percent. Chip-linked names were hit hardest, with Advantest down 12.9 percent, Tokyo Electron 12.5 percent, SK Hynix 11.1 percent and Samsung Electronics 9.9 percent. Investors also expect tighter AI regulation after Democrats' sweeping US midterm wins.

items.en: Rescuers search for dozens trapped in flooded Indonesia gold mine
items.zh: 印尼金礦淹水，26 名礦工受困地底
items.summary: Rescuers in Indonesia are searching for 26 workers still trapped in an unauthorised open-pit gold mine in the Pongkor area of Bogor district, West Java, about 60km south of Jakarta, police said on Wednesday. The site flooded after a nearby river burst its banks following heavy rain on Monday. The Jakarta Search and Rescue Office said the workers are roughly 100 metres underground, and that the shaft's depth, narrow access, slippery ground and poor lighting are complicating the operation while teams monitor water levels. Illegal small-scale mining frequently causes deadly accidents in Indonesia; about 30 nearby pits were closed last week.

items.en: China's Huawei found guilty of trade secrets conspiracy, fraud in US trial
items.zh: 美陪審團裁定華為竊密與銀行詐欺罪成
items.summary: A US jury convicted Huawei Technologies of conspiracy to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, while acquitting the Chinese telecom giant of the most serious charge of criminal racketeering conspiracy. The verdict followed a trial lasting more than two months in which prosecutors called over 60 witnesses, alleging Huawei repeatedly stole technology from rivals including Cisco, Quintel, CNEX, T-Mobile and Fujitsu, and misled banks about business in Iran. Huawei's lawyers said they will appeal, calling the racketeering acquittal a vindication that repudiated the government's central narrative. The case dates to 2018 and the detention of CFO Meng Wanzhou in Canada.

items.en: Australia warns tech giants of multibillion-dollar fines for online 'harm'
items.zh: 澳洲擬對科技巨頭開罰全球營收 5%
items.summary: Australia detailed a proposed digital duty of care law that would fine technology platforms up to 5 percent of global revenue for failing to remove harmful content, a sharp increase from the previously floated AU$109m cap. Agreed between the Labor government and the Greens in the Senate, the bill is expected to pass parliament this week and would replace a patchwork of industry codes covering messaging apps, search engines and AI chatbots. Targeted harms include child sexual abuse material, non-consensual deepfake nudes and terrorism, and Australians aged 16 and over could switch off algorithmic feeds. Industry groups oppose the ministerial discretion it grants.

items.en: US grants SpaceX approval for 1 million space data centres
items.zh: FCC 批准 SpaceX 百萬座太空資料中心
items.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission approved SpaceX's plan to deploy orbital data centres, branded Starmind, authorising up to one million orbital compute modules to process data for use on Earth. The FCC called the licence a first in US history, with chairman Brendan Carr describing it as a bold new frontier for the computing infrastructure needed to support American leadership in artificial intelligence. Elon Musk said the decision would be a great asset to America and the world. Analysts noted only about 17,000 satellites are currently in orbit and that operators routinely seek more approvals than they deploy; Amazon's Leo unit has criticised the proposal.

items.en: Senegal reinstated as 2025 Africa Cup of Nations winners over Morocco
items.zh: 仲裁庭判塞內加爾奪回非洲盃冠軍
items.summary: The Court of Arbitration for Sport upheld Senegal's appeal and restored their 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title, stripping the trophy that the Confederation of African Football had reassigned to Morocco. Senegal beat the hosts 1-0 in the Rabat final on 18 January, but CAF ruled in March that they had forfeited by walking off for roughly 14 minutes in protest at a VAR-awarded penalty, recording a 3-0 win for Morocco. Brahim Diaz missed that penalty and Pape Gueye scored in extra time. The three-member CAS panel led by Gerald Simon found the referee committed no error of law.

items.en: Records tumble as Indian teen Sooryavanshi smashes 53-ball 204 against UAE
items.zh: 印度 15 歲少年 53 球轟 204 分破紀錄
items.summary: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hit 204 off 53 balls for India A against the United Arab Emirates in an Asia Cup Rising Stars match, breaking several List A records. He reached his century off 28 balls, one quicker than Jake Fraser-McGurk's mark, passed 150 in 40 balls and 200 in 52, beating Chad Bowes's 103-ball double-century. His 28 sixes are the most in a senior men's innings, and India chased 250 inside 14.2 overs. Captain Tilak Varma called it absolute carnage. Sooryavanshi became India's youngest men's international in July and led this year's IPL run-scoring.

items.en: Arsenal and Dortmund draw 1-1 as Gyokeres goes from hero to villain
items.zh: 兵工廠 1:1 多特蒙德，約克雷斯先功後過
items.summary: Arsenal were held 1-1 by Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League league phase at the Emirates. Viktor Gyokeres, preferred to Kai Havertz by Mikel Arteta, opened the scoring in the 10th minute with a dipping 25-yard strike, then headed wide from close range late on after a Martin Odegaard cross. Maximilian Beier equalised in the 55th minute, slipping past Gabriel Magalhaes to finish past stand-in goalkeeper Kepa Arrizabalaga, who replaced the injured David Raya. Arsenal twice struck the woodwork and a Jobe Bellingham goal was ruled offside. Arsenal sit fifth after five games, Dortmund seventh.

items.en: 'We need to be seen': Over a third of UK Muslim students face Islamophobia
items.zh: 英國逾三成穆斯林學生遭遇歧視
items.summary: A Federation of Student Islamic Societies report found 38 percent of Muslim students at UK universities have experienced Islamophobia, up from about 25 percent in 2005. The survey of 715 students at 63 universities found women targeted more often than men, 42 percent against 34 percent, rising to 53 percent of Muslim women at Russell Group institutions. Sixty-eight percent of those affected felt unable to report incidents, and 45 percent said Islamophobia moderately or heavily affected their mental health. Three in five feared expressing views on Palestine. FOSIS urges universities to adopt an Islamophobia definition, train staff and protect Friday prayers.

items.en: US Education Department probes Virginia schools after sexual abuse scandal
items.zh: 美教育部調查維州學區背景篩查疏失
items.summary: The US Department of Education has opened an investigation into Albemarle County, Virginia, and is withholding funding after the district closed all 29 of its schools on learning that 524 of roughly 2,800 staff had not undergone routine child sexual abuse background screening. About 14,000 students were affected, leaving parents scrambling for childcare and meals. Officials say none of the 524 is suspected of abuse, and 521 have now been fully vetted. Separate cases involve an indicted school counsellor, an arrested teacher and officials charged with failing to report abuse. Education Secretary Linda McMahon said schools must not shield predators.

items.en: Borno school enrolment nearly doubles after years of conflict
items.zh: 奈及利亞博爾諾州就學人數近乎倍增
items.summary: Nigeria's Borno State says school enrolment rose to 1,418,279 learners in 2025 from 766,551 in 2017-2018, after years of Boko Haram violence closed schools across the northeast. Governor Babagana Umara Zulum says 104 new schools have been built and 2,931 classrooms rehabilitated, and that out-of-school numbers have fallen from about 2.2 million to under 800,000, figures Al Jazeera notes cannot be independently verified. A September census counted 1,801,295 learners sector-wide. Officials credit renewed parental confidence, while residents in rural areas such as Gubio cite distance, cost and insecurity, and authorities work to integrate Islamic schooling.

items.en: Nvidia stock cools after Huang's return-driven surge
items.zh: 輝達漲勢降溫，Anthropic 掛牌後累跌 22%
items.summary: Nvidia shares fell more than 5 percent at Tuesday's open after surging 31 percent on Monday on Jensen Huang's reinstatement as chief executive, as sentiment soured on reports of possible new tariffs on China. The company had shed $1.16 trillion in market value when Huang resigned less than two weeks earlier and has since recovered about $952bn of it. Chip and data-centre names slid too, with AMD down over 10 percent, Micron over 8 percent, Broadcom 4.2 percent and CoreWeave 7.6 percent. Anthropic, which opened at $111.50 against an $83 IPO price, has fallen 22 percent, including 7.3 percent on Tuesday.

items.en: US adds Megaspeed to trade blacklist as Nvidia's Huang returns as CEO
items.zh: 美將 Megaspeed 等七家公司列入管制
items.summary: The US Bureau of Industry and Security added Singapore-based Megaspeed International and six other Southeast Asian firms to its Entity List hours after Jensen Huang returned as Nvidia's chief executive, saying they acted contrary to US national security interests. Shipping advanced US technology to them, including Nvidia's top-end GPUs, now requires an export licence. The other firms are MSFusion, PT Megaspeed International, Speedmatrix, Apex Enterprise Solutions, Swiftdata and Megaspeed Thailand. US officials accuse Megaspeed's former top executive, Alice Huang, of working with China's Ministry of State Security, claims Beijing called groundless. Megaspeed, under DOJ investigation over alleged chip diversion, says it is a lawful business.

items.en: UN chief calls for world to agree on AI oversight within a year
items.zh: 聯合國籲一年內建立 AI 監管框架
items.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged member states to agree within a year on a globally inclusive, principles-based multilateral framework for managing artificial intelligence risks, backed by independent and credible oversight. Speaking at the Bridgetown Special Summit on AI Safety in Barbados, he suggested countries start with shared safety measures, a testing regime and basic requirements for independent supervision, and argued that global institutions still reflect the world of 1945. Guterres, whose term ends in December, said he will advise his successor that controlling AI is essential. Anthropic's Dario Amodei, OpenAI's Sam Altman and Elon Musk have urged slowing development; Nvidia's Jensen Huang and Meta's Mark Zuckerberg favour speed.

items.en: Kenshi Yonezu brings 'GHOST' world tour to Taipei Dome on December 26-27, 2026
items.zh: 米津玄師台北大巨蛋 12/26、27 連唱兩場
items.summary: Kenshi Yonezu's KENSHI YONEZU 2026-2027 WORLD TOUR / GHOST opens its overseas leg at Taipei Dome on December 26 and 27, 2026, with doors at 15:00 and showtime at 18:00 both nights. Taiwan is the first stop outside Japan, ahead of Seoul and Singapore in January 2027 and North America and Europe in February. Tickets, sold via Ticket Plus with real-name registration, are priced from NT$1,800 to NT$5,980, plus accessible seats at NT$2,240 and NT$2,840. After CTBC and Taiwan Mobile presales in late October and a registration lottery drawn November 2, a general sale was slated for November 19 at 12:00, subject to remaining inventory.

items.en: Ado to perform new song 'Bibayataramaetta' as opening theme for TV anime 'Youchien WARS'
items.zh: Ado 新曲獻唱《幼稚園 WARS》片頭曲
items.summary: Billboard Japan announced on November 25, 2026 that Ado will perform a new song, Bibayataramaetta, as the opening theme for the TV anime Youchien WARS, which begins broadcasting in April 2027. The series adapts Yuki Chiba's Shonen Jump+ manga, a violence-meets-romantic-comedy story about criminals who become special teachers guarding the children of world leaders at a so-called black kindergarten. No single release date has been given yet. The news follows Ado's announcement of Ado's Utattemita Tour 2027, six Japanese arena shows opening January 10, 2027 in Tokyo and running through Osaka and Nagoya.

items.en: Official HIGE DANdism release 'Evergreen' for Pokemon's 30th anniversary
items.zh: 髭男寶可夢 30 週年曲 12/1 上線
items.summary: On November 24, 2026, Official HIGE DANdism announced Evergreen, a new song written for Pokemon's 30th anniversary and serving as the culmination of the year-long Pokemon to Tsuzuku campaign. The track will be released as a digital single on December 1, 2026. A special music video premieres one day earlier, on November 30 at 23:00 Japan time, on the official Pokemon YouTube channel, with animation produced by MADHOUSE and directed by Naoko Yamada. The band said they wrote the song to express their personal feelings toward a franchise that has been part of their lives since childhood. A dedicated campaign site has also opened.

items.en: Aimyon announces 6th album 'Smile Shukan' for January 27, 2027
items.zh: 愛繆第六張專輯《微笑週間》1/27 發行
items.summary: Reported November 19, 2026, Aimyon will release her sixth full-length album Smile Shukan on January 27, 2027, her first album in roughly two years and four months. The 13-track record collects drama and commercial tie-ups including Sanagara Lonely, Orange Juice, Koi wa Maboroshi, Ichi ni Tsuite and her 18th single Venus Belt. The first-press limited 2CD edition (4,700 yen) adds a nine-track acoustic disc, Kaze to Ribbon 2, recorded at the Taro Okamoto Memorial Museum in October 2026. Early pre-orders placed between November 19 and December 13 receive an original pouch, with separate store-exclusive bonuses from AIM STORE, Rakuten Books and Tower Records.

items.en: Mrs. GREEN APPLE's album 'POPS' gets a limited clear-green 2LP vinyl edition
items.zh: 《POPS》2027/3 推出透明綠雙黑膠
items.summary: Billboard Japan reported on November 25, 2026 that Mrs. GREEN APPLE will issue their sixth studio album POPS on analog vinyl for the first time. The release is a 2LP set containing all 16 album tracks, split eight per record, pressed on clear green coloured vinyl as a limited-quantity run. It is scheduled for March 24, 2027, and pre-orders are already open. POPS launched the band's Phase 3 era and was released worldwide simultaneously in late September 2026. The vinyl announcement arrives while the group is in the middle of its 28-date Japanese SHADOWS tour, which runs through December 28, 2026.
